verdict.strongest_covered_cluster: The strongest cluster is live execution and streaming: API intake, authentication, scheduler handoff, iterative model/tool execution, identical fan-out to the client and durable event log, replay/reattach, and interruption into a resumable checkpoint are all represented at least recognizably.
verdict.most_consequential_gap: The most consequential gap is the runner lifecycle and recovery contract: capacity-aware residency/isolation placement, idle or suspended runner release, capacity return after crash, bounded replay, and resume/continuation across hosts are absent or only weakly implied.
verdict.coverage_summary: The board inventories nearly all major subject areas and clearly covers the central model/tool loop, live streaming with durable fan-out, basic checkpointing, quota pause behavior, and old-version draining. However, many of the brief's defining qualifiers and failure semantics are missing: placement constraints, disconnect independence, checkpoint contents and retention, suspension/release behavior, bounded crash replay, uncertain tool outcomes, detailed child budgeting/results, quota dimensions, and complete event-log contents. Weighted coverage is therefore below one half, and multiple absent system-defining requirements trigger the RC 6 cap, though the raw rubric score is already lower.
